title: What Happens When You Get a Stitch in Your Side?
description:
Send this to the friend who always gets a stitch five minutes into a run.
In a survey of 965 athletes, 75% of swimmers and 69% of runners had a side stitch in the past year, even though swimming barely jolts your organs (Morton & Callister, Sports Medicine 2015). That review's best explanation is an irritated belly lining, but the cause is still debated. Cleveland Clinic says it's usually nothing to worry about; their tips: slow down, breathe deep, press on the spot, and skip big meals about two hours before exercise.
Next Body File: what happens if you don't brush your teeth for a week.
